description: Interdisciplinary Multi-Language Community Resilience Simulation using Simple Run-Time Infrastructure (SRTI) is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Sherif El-Tawil, University of Michigan (umich.edu). Extreme natural hazards, such as severe earthquakes and hurricanes, can trigger inter-dependencies between the critical infrastructure systems of society, including the built environment (e.g., buildings and bridges), elements of social organization (e.g., social power and cohesion), and institutional arrangements (e.g., policies, politics, economics, and disaster mitigation). Such inter-dependencies can adversely influence community resilience, i.e. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-ycra-9v54. Keywords: Community Resilience, Distributed Computing, Risk Assessment, Interdependecies. Published 2020-10-08. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
